title: Air India and Tourism Ministry Partner to Promote India as Global Destination
excerpt: The non-binding MoU will see co-branded campaigns under the Incredible India brand, leveraging Air India's network across 40 international destinations to boost inbound tourism.
body:
• India's Ministry of Tourism and Air India signed a non-binding MoU to jointly promote the country under the Incredible India brand through co-branded campaigns and destination storytelling.
  • Air India's network of 40 international destinations and 1,000+ connected cities will serve as a key channel for reaching potential tourists across five continents.
  • The partnership includes plans for transit tourism programmes at Delhi and Mumbai hubs, loyalty programme tie-ins, and branding across Air India's aircraft and in-flight media.
  • A Joint Working Group will oversee implementation of the two-year agreement, which carries no financial commitment from either party.

India's Ministry of Tourism and Air India have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to jointly promote the country as a premier global tourism destination under the Incredible India brand. The agreement, signed on July 27 in New Delhi, establishes a framework for coordinated marketing, destination branding, and trade engagement aimed at boosting international tourist arrivals.

The MoU was signed in the presence of Union Minister for Tourism and Culture Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, alongside senior officials including Bhuvnesh Kumar, Secretary of the Ministry of Tourism, and Nipun Aggarwal, Chief Commercial Officer of Air India.

What the Partnership Covers

The collaboration spans tourism promotion, content development, international marketing, and stakeholder engagement. Under the agreement, both organisations will undertake co-branded global promotional campaigns and explore destination storytelling across digital and offline platforms.

Tourism-related content highlighting India's attractions will be developed and showcased through Air India's customer touchpoints, including its in-flight entertainment systems. The two sides will also explore branding opportunities across the airline's platforms — aircraft livery, boarding passes, and in-flight media — subject to feasibility and mutual agreement.

"As the airline that proudly carries India in its name, Air India has a unique responsibility to showcase the country to the world and serve as an ambassador for the new India that is confident, vibrant, warm, and welcoming."

— Nipun Aggarwal, Chief Commercial Officer, Air India

Leveraging Air India's Global Network

Air India currently serves 40 international destinations across five continents, with 25 codeshare partnerships and more than 120 interline agreements connecting India to over 1,000 destinations worldwide. The airline's network covers North America, the UK and Europe, Australia, Africa, and Asia — regions home to roughly 95 percent of the world's population.

The Ministry views this reach as a significant channel for taking India's tourism story to international audiences. The airline's new fleet of world-class aircraft, digital platforms, and global commercial presence will serve as vehicles for the Incredible India campaign.

Transit Tourism and Loyalty Tie-ins

As Air India continues to develop its hubs at Delhi and Mumbai into major international gateways, the MoU includes provisions for encouraging transit and stopover tourism. Both organisations will explore stopover programmes designed to give connecting passengers a taste of India's cultural and heritage offerings.

The partnership will also explore alignment with Air India's Maharaja Club loyalty programme, potentially offering members incentives linked to tourism experiences, including access to cultural attractions, heritage sites, and museums across the country.

"This MoU reflects months of close collaboration and a shared belief that aviation and tourism can be powerful partners in advancing India's global profile."

— P. Balaji, Group Head – Governance, Risk, Compliance & Corporate Affairs, Air India

Implementation and Timeline

A Joint Working Group comprising representatives from both the Ministry and Air India will oversee implementation, identify new areas of collaboration, and periodically review progress. The agreement is valid for an initial period of two years, with a possible one-year extension by mutual consent.

The Ministry emphasised that the partnership is non-commercial, non-binding, and non-exclusive, with no financial commitment from either party. Both sides will also engage with State Tourism Boards and tourism stakeholders to promote destinations across the country through international roadshows, tourism exhibitions, and familiarisation trips.

What's Next

The immediate focus will be on launching joint marketing campaigns and establishing the working group structure. With India targeting a significant increase in inbound tourism over the coming years, the collaboration positions Air India's expanding network as a core channel for the country's destination-marketing strategy. The success of the partnership will likely be measured by its impact on international tourist arrivals and the visibility of the Incredible India brand in key overseas markets.
